title: Motor Imagery ataset from Ofner et al 2017
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 15 healthy subjects performing and imagining six different upper limb movements (elbow flexion/extension, forearm supination/pronation, hand open/close) plus rest conditions. Data were collected during both movement execution and motor imagery sessions using 61-channel EEG with low-frequency filtering (0.3-3 Hz). The dataset is designed for brain-computer interface applications, particularly for neuroprosthesis control, and includes classification results demonstrating significant discrimination between movement types and rest states.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 61 channels at 512 Hz sampling rate using g.tec medical engineering hardware with active sensors. Data were filtered with an 8th order Chebyshev bandpass filter (0.01-200 Hz) and 50 Hz notch filter. Reference electrode was placed at the right mastoid with ground at AFz. Subjects performed sustained upper limb movements in a movement execution session and kinesthetic motor imagery in a separate session, with visual cue presentation at 2 seconds and 3-second trial duration. Classification was performed using shrinkage LDA with discriminative spatial patterns and source localization via sLORETA.
